He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa Hawkeyes]]. ==Early life== Cook has an older brother.{{Citation needed|date=June 2024}} Cook played for [[Chaminade College Preparatory School (Missouri)|Chaminade College Preparatory School]] alongside [[Jayson Tatum]]. As a senior, the duo led the team to a state title, where Cook scored 17 points in the championship game.{{cite news |last1=Emmert |first1=Mark |title=Tyler Cook will get his Big Dance moment, but he also must help the Hawkeyes rediscover their mojo |url=https://www.hawkcentral.com/story/sports/2019/03/12/iowa-basketball-tyler-cook-journey-hawkeyes-ncaa-tournament-march-madness-chaminade-prep-st-louis/3141281002/ |access-date=March 29, 2019 |work=Hawk Central |date=March 12, 2019}} In 2015, Cook announced his intentions to attend the [[University of Iowa]].{{cite news|last1=Palermo|first1=Gregg|title=Chaminade's Tyler Cook tweets college pick|url=http://fox2now.com/2015/09/23/chaminades-tyler-cook-tweets-college-pick/|access-date=May 5, 2018|work=[[FOX2now]]|date=September 23, 2015}}{{cite news|last1=Polacek|first1=Scott|title=Tyler Cook to Iowa: Hawkeyes Land 4-Star PF Prospect|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2571388-tyler-cook-to-iowa-hawkeyes-land-4-star-pf-prospect|access-date=May 5, 2018|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=September 24, 2015}} ==College career== He entered the starting lineup straight away during his freshman season but fractured his right index finger in November and missed seven games.{{cite news|title=Tyler Cook shines for struggling Iowa hoops team|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/02/08/tyler-cook-shines-for-struggling-iowa-hoops-team/110229842/|access-date=May 5, 2018|work=[[USA Today]]|date=February 8, 2018}}{{cite news|last1=Duber|first1=Vinnie|title=Hawkeyes freshman Tyler Cook to miss next three weeks after fracturing finger|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/big-ten/hawkeyes-freshman-tyler-cook-miss-next-three-weeks-after-fracturing-finger|access-date=May 5, 2018|work=[[NBC Sports Chicago]]|date=November 29, 2016}} He averaged 12.3 points and 5.3 rebounds per game on a team that reached the [[2017 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]]. During his sophomore season he averaged 15.3 points and 6.8 rebounds per game.{{cite news|last1=Connors|first1=Ryan|title=Will Tyler Cook return to Iowa basketball next season? 'Only God knows'|url=https://www.landof10.com/iowa/iowa-tyler-cook-transfer-rumors-reports|access-date=May 5, 2018|work=landof10.com|date=March 2, 2018}} In March 2018, Cook submitted paperwork for early entry into the [[2018 NBA draft]], but did not hire an agent.{{cite news|title=Iowa sophomore forward Tyler Cook to test NBA draft interest|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22704997/tyler-cook-iowa-hawkeyes-test-nba-draft-interest|access-date=May 5, 2018|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=Associated Press|date=March 9, 2018}}{{cite news|last1=Johnson|first1=Jeff|title=Tyler Cook claims his departure from Iowa basketball isn't foregone conclusion|url=https://www.thegazette.com/hawkeye-basketball/tyler-cook-claims-his-departure-from-iowa-basketball-isnt-foregone-conclusion/|access-date=May 5, 2018|work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]]|date=April 11, 2018}}{{cite news|last1=Petaros|first1=Nick|title=Iowa basketball: Cook embraces defensive role|url=https://wcfcourier.com/sports/college/iowa/iowa-basketball-cook-embraces-defensive-role/article_8dcec7db-2a94-5efb-a24e-a115a35da4f1.html|access-date=May 5, 2018|work=[[The Waterloo-Cedar Falls Courier]]|date=July 17, 2016}} Cook scored 26 points as the Hawkeyes defeated [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]] to win the [[2K Sports Classic|2K Classic tournament]]. He had another 26 as Iowa beat their rivals [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]]. Cook missed a game against [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]] on January 9, 2019, with a knee injury, though the team won without him.{{cite news |first=Mike |last=Hlas| title=Without Tyler Cook, Iowa men's basketball still beats Northwestern |url=https://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/hawkeyes/iowa-mens-basketball/iowa-northwestern-basketball-final-score-jan-9-2019-stats-recap-20190110 |access-date=March 4, 2019 |work=The Gazette |date=January 9, 2019}} As a junior, Cook led Iowa to the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and averaged 14.5 points and 7.6 rebounds per game. Cook declared for the NBA draft and hired an agent.{{cite news |last1=Emmert |first1=Mark |title=Hawkeye basketball team already looking ahead: 'We'll be back. I promise you that.' |url=https://www.hawkcentral.com/story/sports/2019/03/25/iowa-basketball-season-in-review-preview-2019-20-nicholas-baer-joe-wieskamp/3257681002/ |access-date=March 29, 2019 |work=Hawk Central |date=March 25, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2019–2020)=== After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]], Cook signed a partially guaranteed contract with the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Tyler-Cook-36403/high-school-60034|title=Tyler Cook, Chaminade, Power Forward|website=247Sports|language=en-US|access-date=April 25, 2018}} On August 13, 2019, Cook signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Nuggets.{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets sign Tyler Cook and P.J. Dozier|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-sign-tyler-cook-pj-dozier-081319|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 13, 2019|date=August 13, 2019}} However, he was later released on October 16, 2019, during training camp.{{cite web|title=We have released forward Tyler Cook.|url=https://twitter.com/nuggets/status/1184578045354500097|date=October 16, 2019|website=Denver Nuggets on Twitter.com|access-date=October 16, 2019}} Cook was later claimed off waivers by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on October 19.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Claim Tyler Cook off Waivers|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/tyler-cook-claimed-191019|date=October 19, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 19, 2019}} On January 3, 2020, the Cavaliers announced that they had converted the two-way contract with Cook to a standard NBA contract.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Convert Contract of Tyler Cook|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cook-standard-contract-200103|date=January 3, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 3, 2020}} On January 6, the Cavaliers announced that they had waived Cook.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/waive-mckinnie-cook-200106|title=Cavaliers Sign Levi Randolph; Waive McKinnie, Cook|date=January 6, 2020|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 6, 2020}} On January 9, Cook was re-signed by the Cavaliers, and immediately assigned to the [[Canton Charge]].{{Cite web|url= https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cook-10-day-200109|title= Cavs Sign Tyler Cook To 10-Day Contract|date=January 9, 2020|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 9, 2020}} On January 20, the Cavaliers announced that they had signed a second 10-day contract with Cook.{{cite web|title=Cavs Sign Tyler Cook To Second 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cook-second-10-day-200120|date=January 20, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 20, 2020}} ===Canton Charge (2020)=== Cook's contract was not renewed when the second 10-day deal expired. He rejoined the Charge.{{cite news |last1=Popovich |first1=Mike |title=Tyler Cook hopes Cavs experience benefits him in his return to Canton Charge |url=https://www.cantonrep.com/sports/20200131/tyler-cook-hopes-cavs-experience-benefits-him-in-his-return-to-canton-charge |access-date=February 2, 2020 |work=[[Canton Repository]] |date=January 31, 2020}} ===Oklahoma City Blue (2020)=== On February 16, 2020, the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] announced that they had acquired Cook with a first-round draft pick and a second-round draft pick in [[2021 NBA G League draft (January)|2020 NBA G League draft]] from the Canton Charge in exchange of [[Vincent Edwards (basketball)|Vincent Edwards]] and two 2020 first-round draft picks.{{cite web|title=Oklahoma City Blue Acquires Tyler Cook|url=https://oklahomacity.gleague.nba.com/news/oklahoma-city-blue-acquires-tyler-cook|date=February 16, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 16, 2020}} On February 26, Cook registered 19 points, two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block in a 128–115 win over the [[Northern Arizona Suns]].{{cite news |title=Tyler Cook: Leads team in scoring |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/tyler-cook-leads-team-in-scoring/ |access-date=June 14, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 27, 2020}} ===Denver Nuggets (2020)=== On June 30, 2020, the Denver Nuggets announced that they had signed Cook to a two-way contract.{{cite web|title=Nuggets sign Tyler Cook to Two-Way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-tyler-cook-20200630|date=June 30, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=June 30, 2020}} ===Iowa Wolves (2021)=== On November 30, 2020, the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] announced that they had signed Cook,{{cite web|title=Timberwolves sign Tyler Cook|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-tyler-cook|date=December 2, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 2, 2020}} but on December 19, 2020, the Timberwolves waived Cook.{{cite web|title=Timberwolves waive four players|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-waive-four-players|date=December 19, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 19, 2020}} On January 8, 2021, the [[Iowa Wolves]] announced that they had acquired the returning right to Cook and the 17th overall pick in the [[2021 NBA G League draft (January)|first 2021 NBA G League draft]] from the Oklahoma City Blue for the returning right to [[James Webb III]] and the 7th overall pick in the 2021 draft.{{cite web|title=Wolves Acquire Returning Player Rights of Tyler Cook and Oklahoma City Blue's 2020–2021 First Round 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 8, 2021}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2021)=== On February 24, 2021, Cook was signed to a 10-day contract by the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Tyler Cook to 10-day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/02/24/brooklyn-nets-sign-tyler-cook-10-day-contract |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 24, 2021 |date=February 24, 2021}} ===Detroit Pistons (2021)=== On March 19, 2021, Cook was signed to a 10-day contract by the [[Detroit Pistons]],{{cite web |title=DETROIT PISTONS SIGN TYLER COOK TO 10-DAY CONTRACT |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-tyler-cook-10-day-contract |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 20, 2021 |date=March 19, 2021}} and on March 29, he signed a second 10-day contract.{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons Sign Tyler Cook To Second 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-tyler-cook-second-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 30, 2021|date=March 29, 2021}} Finally, on April 7, he signed a multi-year contract.{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons Sign Tyler Cook to a Multi-Year Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-tyler-cook-multi-year-contract|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 7, 2021|date=April 7, 2021}} On July 31, 2021, Cook was waived by the Pistons.{{cite web|first=Omari|last=Sankofa II|title=Detroit Pistons waive Cory Joseph, Deividas Sirvydis and Tyler Cook ahead of free agency|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2021/07/31/detroit-pistons-waive-cory-joseph-tyer-cook-deividas-sirvydis/5444930001/|website=Detroit Free Press|date=July 31, 2021|access-date=August 1, 2021}} ===Chicago Bulls (2021–2022)=== On September 8, 2021, Cook signed with the Chicago Bulls{{cite web|title=Bulls sign Free Agents|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-free-agents|website=NBA.com|date=September 8, 2021|accessdate=October 3, 2021}} and on October 18, they converted his deal into a two-way contract with the [[Windy City Bulls]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|title=BULLS FINALIZE 2021–22 OPENING NIGHT ROSTER|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-finalize-2021-22-opening-night-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2021|access-date=October 22, 2021}} ===Salt Lake City Stars (2022–2023)=== On October 23, 2022, Cook joined the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] training camp roster.{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/stars-announce-2022-23-training-camp-roster/n-5892964|title=Stars Announce 2022-23 Training Camp Roster|website=oursportscentral.com|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=October 23, 2022}} ===South East Melbourne Phoenix (2023)=== On September 11, 2023, Cook signed with the [[South East Melbourne Phoenix]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) as an injury replacement for [[Alan Williams (basketball)|Alan Williams]].{{cite web|title=Williams sidelined, NBA forward in|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/williams-sidelined-nba-forward-in|website=NBL.com.au|date=September 11, 2023|access-date=September 11, 2023}} He was named the most valuable player of the NBL pre-season tournament.{{cite web|title=Thank You Tyler Cook|url=https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/thank-you-tyler-cook|website=semphoenix.com.au|date=October 18, 2023|access-date=October 18, 2023}} He suffered an eye injury in his third game and subsequently missed the next two. Upon Williams' return from injury on October 18, Cook was released by the Phoenix.{{cite web|title=Star big man returns for Phoenix|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/star-big-man-returns-for-phoenix|website=NBL.com.au|date=October 18, 2023|access-date=October 18, 2023}} ===Joventut Badalona (2023–2024)=== On November 16, 2023,
